new.vignette: A 13-year-old boy has persistent Epstein-Barr virus viremia, recurrent lymphadenopathy, and reduced cytotoxic activity of natural killer cells. Flow cytometry shows markedly decreased NKG2D on NK cells and CD8+ T cells. Sequencing identifies a loss-of-function variant in MAGT1. Immunoblotting of patient lymphocytes shows underglycosylated NKG2D protein with reduced steady-state expression.
new.lead_in: Which cellular process is most directly impaired by this mutation?

options.A: N-linked glycosylation of selected proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum
options.B: O-linked glycosylation of proteins in the Golgi apparatus
options.C: TAP-dependent transport of cytosolic peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum
options.D: Proteasomal degradation of ubiquitinated cytosolic proteins
options.E: Attachment of glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchors to proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum

new.tested_construct: MAGT1 deficiency causes selective defects in N-linked glycosylation, including hypoglycosylation and reduced expression of NKG2D
new.educational_objective: Recognize MAGT1 deficiency as a selective N-linked glycosylation disorder in which NKG2D hypoglycosylation reduces NKG2D expression and compromises cytotoxic lymphocyte function.

existing.vignette: A 9-year-old boy has recurrent bacterial respiratory infections and bronchiectasis. Flow cytometry shows markedly reduced HLA class I expression on nucleated cells, preserved HLA class II expression, and a low CD8+ T-cell count with a normal CD4+ T-cell count. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in TAP2.
existing.lead_in: Which intracellular step is most directly impaired by this defect?

options.A: Proteasomal cleavage of cytosolic proteins into peptide fragments
options.B: Removal of invariant-chain-derived peptide from MHC class II molecules in acidified endosomes
options.C: Transport of newly synthesized MHC class II molecules from the endoplasmic reticulum to endosomal compartments
options.D: ATP-dependent transport of cytosolic peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum for loading onto MHC class I molecules
options.E: Endocytosis of extracellular proteins for presentation to CD4+ T cells

existing.tested_construct: TAP1/TAP2 transport cytosolic peptides into the ER for MHC class I loading
existing.educational_objective: TAP1/TAP2 use ATP to transport cytosolic peptides into the ER for MHC class I loading; TAP deficiency lowers surface MHC I and can produce selective CD8+ T-cell lymphopenia.

new.vignette: A 27-year-old man has recurrent episodes of confusion after carbohydrate-rich meals. During an episode, plasma ammonia and citrulline are markedly elevated. He has a longstanding preference for protein- and fat-rich foods. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC25A13.
new.lead_in: Which mitochondrial transport process is most directly impaired?

options.A: Import of ornithine from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix
options.B: Export of aspartate from the mitochondrial matrix in exchange for glutamate plus a proton
options.C: Export of carbamoyl phosphate from the mitochondrial matrix into the cytosol
options.D: Import of pyruvate from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix
options.E: Export of acetyl-CoA directly across the inner mitochondrial membrane

new.tested_construct: Citrin is the mitochondrial aspartate-glutamate carrier that exports aspartate to the cytosol while importing glutamate plus a proton
new.educational_objective: Link SLC25A13/citrin deficiency to loss of mitochondrial aspartate export, impaired malate-aspartate shuttling, and reduced cytosolic aspartate availability for the urea cycle.

existing.vignette: A child develops episodic confusion and vomiting after high-protein meals. Plasma ammonia and ornithine are elevated, and urine contains homocitrulline. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in SLC25A15.
existing.lead_in: Which transport process is most directly impaired?

options.A: Export of citrulline from the mitochondrial matrix to the cytosol
options.B: Import of pyruvate into the mitochondrial matrix
options.C: Export of aspartate from mitochondria through the malate-aspartate shuttle
options.D: Import of long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria through the carnitine shuttle
options.E: Import of ornithine from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix

existing.tested_construct: SLC25A15 encodes ORNT1, the mitochondrial ornithine transporter that moves cytosolic ornithine into the mitochondrial matrix. Loss deprives the urea cycle of intramitochondrial ornithine, causing hyperammonemia, hyperornithinemia, and homocitrullinuria.
existing.educational_objective: Link HHH syndrome to defective mitochondrial ornithine import through SLC25A15/ORNT1.

new.vignette: A newborn develops recurrent seizures that persist despite phenobarbital and levetiracetam but stop after intravenous pyridoxine. Urine and plasma contain markedly increased alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde and piperideine-6-carboxylate. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in ALDH7A1.
new.lead_in: Which biochemical mechanism most directly explains the pyridoxine dependence?

options.A: Failure to oxidize pyridoxine phosphate to pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate because of PNPO deficiency
options.B: Competitive inhibition of glutamate decarboxylase by accumulated alpha-ketoglutarate
options.C: Condensation of accumulated piperideine-6-carboxylate with pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate, functionally inactivating the cofactor
options.D: Failure of intestinal vitamin B6 absorption because of loss of a sodium-dependent pyridoxine transporter
options.E: Accelerated renal excretion of pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate caused by proximal tubular dysfunction

new.tested_construct: ALDH7A1 deficiency causes P6C accumulation, which chemically condenses with and inactivates pyridoxal 5-prime-phosphate
new.educational_objective: Recognize pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy due to ALDH7A1 deficiency as a lysine-catabolism disorder in which accumulated P6C chemically inactivates PLP.

existing.vignette: A 6-year-old boy has progressive bowing of the legs, short stature, bone pain, and recurrent dental abscesses. Serum phosphate is low with renal phosphate wasting; serum calcium is normal. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic variant in PHEX.
existing.lead_in: Which of the following downstream changes most directly causes this patient's renal phosphate wasting?

options.A: Excess parathyroid hormone causing internalization of proximal-tubular sodium-phosphate cotransporters
options.B: Loss of the SLC34A3 sodium-phosphate cotransporter reducing proximal-tubular phosphate uptake
options.C: Reduced intestinal phosphate absorption caused by loss of the vitamin D receptor
options.D: Generalized proximal-tubule dysfunction causing urinary glucose and amino-acid loss
options.E: FGF23-mediated internalization of proximal-tubular sodium-phosphate cotransporters

existing.tested_construct: PHEX loss of function increases FGF23 activity. Excess FGF23 reduces proximal-tubular phosphate reabsorption by promoting internalization of sodium-phosphate cotransporters and also lowers calcitriol synthesis, producing chronic phosphate wasting and defective bone mineralization.
existing.educational_objective: Connect PHEX deficiency with excess FGF23 and proximal-tubular sodium-phosphate cotransporter internalization in X-linked hypophosphatemia.

new.vignette: A 5-month-old infant has poor growth, chronic diarrhea, recurrent Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, and megaloblastic anemia with pancytopenia. Serum folate and cerebrospinal-fluid 5-methyltetrahydrofolate are both very low, whereas vitamin B12 is normal. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC46A1.
new.lead_in: Which transport defect most directly explains both the systemic and neurologic folate deficiency?

options.A: Loss of folate receptor-alpha-mediated uptake at the choroid plexus with preserved intestinal folate absorption
options.B: Loss of intrinsic-factor-dependent cobalamin uptake in the terminal ileum
options.C: Loss of the reduced folate carrier that mediates folate entry into systemic tissues at near-neutral pH
options.D: Loss of proton-coupled folate transport across the apical proximal small intestine and at the choroid plexus
options.E: Loss of intracellular folylpolyglutamate synthesis that normally retains folates within cells

new.tested_construct: SLC46A1 encodes the proton-coupled folate transporter required for intestinal folate absorption and for folate transport into cerebrospinal fluid
new.educational_objective: Distinguish hereditary folate malabsorption from isolated cerebral folate disorders by recognizing that SLC46A1/PCFT is required for both proximal-intestinal folate absorption and transport of folate into cerebrospinal fluid.

existing.vignette: A 3-year-old girl who developed normally during infancy has progressive gait instability, tremor, seizures, and loss of previously acquired language. MRI shows cerebral hypomyelination. Hemoglobin, mean corpuscular volume, and serum folate are normal. Cerebrospinal fluid 5-methyltetrahydrofolate is markedly reduced. Genetic testing identifies biallelic FOLR1 pathogenic variants.
existing.lead_in: Which transport process is primarily impaired?

options.A: Intestinal folate uptake across the apical enterocyte membrane
options.B: Folate transport across the choroid plexus into cerebrospinal fluid
options.C: Cellular vitamin B12 uptake through intrinsic-factor receptors in the terminal ileum
options.D: Glucose transport across blood-brain-barrier endothelial cells

existing.tested_construct: FOLR1 encodes folate receptor alpha at the choroid plexus. Loss of function impairs folate transport across the blood-choroid-plexus-CSF barrier, producing very low CSF folate despite normal systemic folate and later-onset developmental regression, seizures, movement abnormalities, and hypomyelination.
existing.educational_objective: Distinguish FOLR1 cerebral folate transport deficiency from systemic folate deficiency by recognizing very low CSF folate with normal serum folate and blood counts.

new.vignette: A 10-month-old boy develops lethargy and tachypnea during a viral illness. Laboratory studies show hyperammonemia, lactic acidosis, hypoglycemia, and urinary metabolites suggesting impaired activity of several mitochondrial carboxylases. Biotinidase activity is normal. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in CA5A, which encodes mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase VA.
new.lead_in: Which molecule is normally generated by the deficient enzyme to support the affected mitochondrial pathways?
new.tested_construct: Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase VA generates bicarbonate that is supplied to CPS1 and multiple mitochondrial carboxylases
new.educational_objective: Recognize CA5A deficiency as impaired mitochondrial bicarbonate generation, simultaneously compromising CPS1 and several biotin-dependent carboxylases.

existing.vignette: A 15-month-old child develops lethargy and hypoketotic hypoglycemia during a viral illness. Examination shows hepatomegaly, and echocardiography demonstrates dilated cardiomyopathy. Plasma free carnitine is markedly reduced. Molecular testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in SLC22A5.
existing.lead_in: Which transport process is directly impaired by this mutation?

options.A: Transport of long-chain fatty acyl groups across the inner mitochondrial membrane by carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase
options.B: Conversion of long-chain acyl-CoA to acylcarnitine by carnitine palmitoyltransferase I
options.C: High-affinity uptake of carnitine into cells through the OCTN2 plasma-membrane transporter
options.D: Conversion of acylcarnitine back to acyl-CoA by carnitine palmitoyltransferase II
options.E: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of medium-chain fatty acyl-CoA by medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase

existing.tested_construct: SLC22A5 encodes the high-affinity OCTN2 carnitine transporter. Loss of OCTN2 impairs cellular carnitine uptake and renal carnitine reabsorption, causing very low plasma and intracellular carnitine and limiting transport of long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria for beta-oxidation.
existing.educational_objective: Link primary carnitine deficiency to SLC22A5/OCTN2-mediated failure of cellular carnitine uptake and renal carnitine reabsorption.
